correctness.rationale: All chain-ring graph adjacencies follow from the valuation inequality. The loopless matrix equations include the high-valuation diagonal subtraction. Every kernel vector has constant high-class coordinates with uniquely determined partial sums, zero socle, and a single low-coordinate zero-sum constraint, giving rank q^floor(m/2). An exact row combination generates each socle unit coordinate, proving primal distance one; a within-low-layer difference gives dual distance two. The restricted Gram form of the kernel is a zero-sum hyperplane with one-dimensional radical, proving the hull. A standalone elimination test not assuming the claimed rank passed all 16 finite configurations, including p=2 and nonprime q; tests are supplementary, not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The principal theorem gives the first identified all-length, all-residue-field exact prime-characteristic kernel/rank/dual/hull/distance classification for ordinary loopless zero-divisor adjacency row codes of finite commutative chain rings. The exact m=4 odd-prime rank/dual/hull statements are prior work and expressly not claimed as novel. For that case the published minimum-distance-two assertion is incompatible with an explicit socle unit-vector row combination. Closest broad adjacency spectral and real matrix rank results treat different coefficient fields/invariants. Targeted bibliographic and publicly indexed research comparisons revealed no covering theorem. Residual risk of an equivalent unindexed modular adjacency calculation remains.
residual_risks: A matching modular p-rank and high-layer kernel formula may exist in unindexed earlier coding literature or an uninspected full-text appendix; targeted search is not proof of global novelty.

value.rationale: The exact p-characteristic graph-adjacency code and its full dual are natural invariants for finite commutative chain rings. The theorem classifies all nilpotency lengths, residue fields, and mixed-characteristic cases, not a handpicked numerical slice. The higher-length nontrivial dual lifts and one-dimensional hull supply structural information absent from the recent length-four study. The explicit socle weight-one words settle a meaningful coding-theoretic boundary: these adjacency codes cannot detect even one symbol error, correcting a stronger unsupported distance assertion in the motivating example. The result is not promoted as an asymptotically good error-correcting code.
